scenarios.title: Detail screen reflects a backend state change even across a service restart (no stale next action)
scenarios.purpose: Prove the exception detail screen renders from live backend state, not a cached snapshot, so it can never name a next action the backend no longer holds.
scenarios.rationale: AC3 is the heaviest-weighted criterion and workflow_store.py's +163 lines of new reads are where a stale snapshot would hide; a restart is the cleanest way to force any in-process cache to be discarded and to observe whether the rendered screen equals durable state.
scenarios.requirement_reference: the screen never shows a state the backend does not currently hold

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT id, state FROM workflow_runs ORDER BY id LIMIT 5"

persisted_state_checks.name: backend still holds the runs the screen must mirror

scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only against the DB; restarts the shared callback service, so it must not run concurrently with any other :8001 scenario. Does not mutate persisted rows.

scenarios.title: Canonical fresh DB still builds all tables the screen depends on after the schema change
scenarios.purpose: Directly exercise create_canonical_schema (touched by this diff) on a fresh database and confirm it produces the backing tables, so a freshly provisioned backend can actually hold the state the screen shows rather than defaulting.

actions.name: build fresh canonical schema and list tables
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3,tempfile,os,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from freight_recon.schema import create_canonical_schema; p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'probe.sqlite3'); c=sqlite3.connect(p); create_canonical_schema(c); print(sorted(r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")))"

scenarios.isolation_note: Builds a canonical schema in a fresh tempdir created by the probe itself; touches no shared workspace or service.

assumptions: The exception detail screen is served by the 'callback' service on http://127.0.0.1:8001 (the only local app URL and service I was given), and its list/detail routes are '/exceptions' and '/exceptions/{id}'. These paths are a convention guess — the builder's exception_detail_view.py and its route wiring are not present in this working tree, so I could not confirm them.
The running app on :8001 is bound to the driver_probe workspace and reads/writes data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 (the exact DB handed to me as the approved sqlite oracle).
The harness provisions data/active_workspace/driver_probe/ with the app running before scenarios execute; that directory and DB do not exist in my checkout.
'Exception' maps onto a workflow_runs row in a review/exception state, with evidence in audit_events — the model that is present in this tree (migrations/phase2_tenant_first.py).
unresolved_questions: BLOCKER: the builder's changed files (exception_detail_view.py, templates/exception_detail.html, workflow_store.py, authorization.py) and the modified schema.py are not in this working tree, so I could not read the screen's actual route, its rendered literal text, or the new schema columns for owner/next-action/evidence. I therefore avoided asserting screen text as expected_observations (which would false-fail a correct product) and leaned on sqlite oracles plus universal error-marker forbidden_observations.

What is the exact URL for the exception detail screen and its list page, and is it served on :8001 (callback) or on the site server (:8000, out of scope for me)? All request-based scenarios above depend on this and will false-fail if the path differs.

What is the tenant the driver_probe callback server is bound to? Without it I cannot provision a controlled exception row via sqlite INSERT that the screen would find, which blocks a precise before/after ui_backend_disagreement scenario (drive backend state -> observe screen must follow) — the strongest possible AC3 test.

What column/table did schema.py (+31) add to persist 'next action' and 'owner', and what literal strings does the template emit for state, owner, and 'no evidence recorded'? With these I could assert the screen text verbatim and directly verify AC1/AC2/AC3 instead of only asserting the screen renders without crashing.

Is there an approved way to drive an exception through a real state transition (e.g., a resolving action) without minting a signed token from the secret? If so, an idempotency/repeated-request scenario on that transition plus a screen re-read would be high value; I could not author it with the approved command set.
